full_name: AIST — AI Safety Team at Harvard (formerly AISST)
mission: 'The AI Safety Team (AIST, like "aced") is a community of technical and policy researchers at Harvard.' Formerly the AI Safety Student Team (AISST), it runs nine-week technical, policy and AI×biorisk fellowships each semester, member research tracks and joint workshops with MIT AI Alignment (MAIA). Status note: renamed from AISST to AIST. Founding year approximate. For Harvard faculty safety work see Boaz Barak's CS 2881 AI Safety course.

key_work.title: AI 2027 (member/alum co-authored)
key_work.plain_summary: A detailed scenario of how superhuman AI could arrive by 2027; co-author Romeo Dean is highlighted as an AIST member/alum.

key_work.title: Measuring AI Ability to Complete Long Tasks (member co-authored)
key_work.plain_summary: METR's finding that the length of tasks AI agents can complete has been doubling about every seven months; AIST highlights member Nikola Jurkovic as a co-author.

key_work.title: Persona Features Control Emergent Misalignment (member co-authored)
key_work.plain_summary: Finds internal 'persona' features that explain why narrow bad fine-tuning makes models broadly misaligned.

warnings.text: 'We're on track to develop immensely powerful AI soon, and we are woefully unprepared for its arrival' (homepage).
Without safeguards, powerful AI could autonomously escape control, help bad actors build weapons, or slowly take important decisions out of human hands.

recommendations.text: Train students through structured technical, policy and biosecurity fellowships, then involve them in research.
Connect students with professionals at labs and nonprofits (AIST–MAIA workshops).
